generation.prompt: A precise photographic material edit to the FIRST image, the finished allotment illustration. Change only the slim BAMBOO CANES of the low foreground netting frame around the four brassicas. The current rails are improbably ruler-straight. Keep the SIX weathered tennis balls exactly where they are, the same six planted feet, 30cm high framework, same footprint and sound rectilinear construction. Each endpoint must still enter its own hole. At these fixed endpoints the individual shafts have different subtle bows between joints. Across the long and highly visible front horizontal crossbar (between the two nearest tennis balls), insert a real shallow upward arch with the crest left of centre, about one cane thickness (10–12 picture pixels at the supplied 1619px width) above the straight line between the balls. Smoothly return to the right ball with a faint natural change of direction at one node. Give the middle crossbar a shallower bow in the opposite direction; the rear crossbar in John's hands stays mostly straight. One long side rail has a slight sideways sweep, one upright bows gently outward halfway up, other canes are near-straight with subtly uneven diameters, slight taper and occasional nodes. Ordinary sound home-grown bamboo, believable and unobtrusive; no wavy sticks, broken canes, sagging rails, or wobbly structure. The bends should be apparent both in the silhouette against the soil and at the scale of the finished book. Absolutely preserve the four different brassica plants where they are, the bottom-right joint-detail inset, visible joints, grass path and both brick edges, John, working hands and likeness. Inset is a short close-up and needs no change. Keep original still framing, camera position, colour and light. No labels or measurements. Other inputs show the original camera site and John's real lowered profile for reference only; the target image supplies everything else.
